items.title: Prove both gates ignore an item-level withdrawal, repro-first
items.context: Isolated fixture (mkdtemp, never a real story): take it to REVIEW, withdraw one checklist item that SHARES an acceptance binding with a delivered item, then observe story_advance --phase=TEST refused twice - evaluateReviewCompleteness with review_completeness_missing_evidence naming the withdrawn intents, and the channel gate with 'has no dispatch/subagent_result evidence'. Both must be OBSERVED. Include controls: a non-withdrawn item with genuinely missing evidence must still be refused (rules out 'skips everything'), and a fully-covered item must still pass (rules out 'refuses everything'). If either gate already handles item-level withdrawal, the premise is refuted and items 2-5 must be re-scoped rather than executed.
items.userSees: node packages/main/tests/red/red-b45a5-*.mjs prints RED rows for both gates on the pre-fix tree and exits non-zero.

happy.desc: Both gates observed refusing an item-level withdrawal on the pre-fix tree

edge.desc: Positive control: a fully covered item still passes, so 'refuses everything' is ruled out

adversarial.desc: Negative control: a non-withdrawn item with genuinely missing evidence is still refused, so 'skips everything' is ruled out

verificationEvidence.note: Waiver for a SELF-INVALIDATING PIN, not for the property. The pin is selector B45A5-ROW-B3=RED on a command+selector pair that is immutable on first selector-bearing write. CHK-002/CHK-003 flipped B3 to GREEN, which is the entire point of the story, so any re-attestation of this row now derives fail. It can never be re-earned. THE PROPERTY IS STILL PROVEN, by a different and better artifact: red-evidence.json records the pre-fix observation bound to baseline HEAD e66bb0b2 with a runnable failingCommand, and the registered non-optional artifact now runs GREEN on every validate with rows B1/B2/B3 covering exactly this intent plus six controls. LESSON - a NEW VARIANT of the selector rule, distinct from the one that cost B-8df9 a finding. There the selector was a prose line a sibling item legitimately reworded. Here the selector is a stable row id, which obeys that rule, but it pins the RED VERDICT - the exact value the story exists to invert. A red artifacts evidence must never pin its own red state; pin a CONTROL row that survives the fix, or a structural invariant. The same implementer got edge:0 and adversarial:0 right by pinning A1/A2 CONTROL-OK, which still hold. I should have caught this when reviewing CHK-001s evidence rather than at closeout.

Row A1 is the positive control: a fully covered, non-withdrawn fixture is demanded by neither gate (completeness reports no missing-evidence gap, channel reports ok). It rules out refuses-everything, without which the RED rows would be uninterpretable. A BROKEN A1 forces exit 2 and suppresses every B row to NOT-MEASURED, so the artifact cannot report a convenient conclusion over an unsound control.

verificationEvidence.note: Row A2 is the negative control: a NON-withdrawn item with genuinely missing evidence and no dispatch is still refused by both gates. It rules out skips-everything. The negative-control fixture is identical to the subject fixture apart from the authorized withdrawal (row C3 measures that, normalizing only status, decisionRef and endTime), so the two verdicts can only differ because of the withdrawal. Verified live: forcing the channel gate to exempt every item makes A2 BROKEN and the run exits 2 with all B rows NOT-MEASURED.

items.title: Wire evaluateReviewCompleteness to the decision-backed item-level helper
items.context: core/proofstory.ts:2084. The helper withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom(decision) already exists at core/proofstory.ts:1622 and is currently called only by tasks/scope-shrinkage-withdrawal-floor-smoke.ts. Use IT, not a status comparison: it takes the decision record as input, so the backing requirement is structural. Do NOT route this through core/checklist-status.ts - that module has zero decisionRef awareness in its 42 lines, and using it would yield a naive status==='withdrawn' skip that anyone can trigger by editing one JSON field.
items.userSees: A story with a withdrawn item advances; the completeness gate prints pass instead of review_completeness_missing_evidence naming that item.

The same row was RED on the immediately preceding commit, so the subtraction is load-bearing rather than incidental. Selector is the stable row id, not a prose conclusion line.

verificationEvidence.note: Row C1 pins the structural backing this skip depends on: the exclusion set is resolved by withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom from the DECISION RECORD (decision=confirmed, userConfirmed=true) and the applier stamped the item with that same decisionId. The new withdrawnItemIntentRefs helper in core/proofstory.ts takes only (items, decision) and keys membership on withdrawnIds.has(item.id); this commit diff contains no item.status, no isWithdrawnChecklistStatus and no withdrawn string comparison, so nothing added here can be triggered by editing a status field. Full unbacked-state adversarial coverage (absent decisionRef, dangling decisionRef, a decision that lists a DIFFERENT real item, a decision overwritten to rejected) is CHK-004 of this story and is not claimed by this row.

items.title: Give the normal-channel gate the same decision-backed skip
items.context: handlers/validate-channel.ts checkDispatchEvidence, which today has zero status or withdrawal awareness. A withdrawn item must not require dispatch/subagent_result evidence because no work was dispatched by design. Same structural backing as the previous item. Do not weaken the dispatch requirement for any item that is not withdrawn - the normal-channel discipline is correct and must stay strict.
items.userSees: The channel gate prints the withdrawn item as skipped with its decision id rather than 'has no dispatch/subagent_result evidence'.

happy.desc: checkDispatchEvidence does not require dispatch evidence for a decision-backed withdrawn item

edge.desc: Dispatch evidence is still required for every item that is not withdrawn

adversarial.desc: Same structural backing as CHK-002: decision-record routed, never a bare status comparison

verificationEvidence.note: Row B2 is the channel gate measured on the subject fixture, whose only dispatch event covers the delivered item: after the wiring it observes channel ok=true with no offenders and the detail line "withdrawn (SD-...): CHK-002", i.e. the withdrawn item is rendered in its own third bucket with the authorizing decision id instead of "has no dispatch/subagent_result evidence". Row C4 in the same run confirms it is in neither the Covered: nor the plan.md Owner=main-agent exempted: bucket. Reverting only validate-channel.ts and rebuilding puts B2 back to RED while B1 stays GREEN, so this wiring is independently load-bearing. Selector is the stable row id.

items.title: Prove an unbacked withdrawal skips nothing
items.context: This is the anti-bypass deliverable and is as important as the skip. Cover at least: status=withdrawn with NO decisionRef; a decisionRef naming a decision that does not exist; a decisionRef naming a real decision that does NOT list that item; and a decision whose userConfirmed is absent or false. Each must still be refused by both gates. Without these the fix converts a correct gate into a back door.
items.userSees: Editing status to withdrawn by hand, without a real confirmed decision listing that item, still fails both gates.

happy.desc: status=withdrawn with no decisionRef is refused by both gates

edge.desc: A decisionRef naming a nonexistent decision, and one naming a real decision that does not list the item, are both refused

adversarial.desc: A decision overwritten to decision=rejected / userConfirmed=false stops authorizing the skip; states are built by direct JSON write since that is the actual threat model
